blocks.passage:
Working capital is the money a company needs to run its daily business. It pays the salaries, buys the materials and covers the bills while the company waits to get paid.

The idea is simple: there is money coming in from customers, and money going out to suppliers, staff and tax. Working capital is the gap between the two — and how you manage it is often the difference between a healthy company and a stressed one.

Good trade companies watch their working capital every week.

items.q: What is working capital?
options: The money a company needs to run its daily business
items.why: "Working capital is the money a company needs to run its daily business."

items.q: What does working capital pay for?
options: Salaries, materials and bills while waiting to get paid
items.why: "It pays the salaries, buys the materials and covers the bills while the company waits to get paid."

items.q: Working capital is the gap between…
options: money coming in and money going out
items.why: "money coming in from customers, and money going out… Working capital is the gap between the two."

items.q: What can managing working capital be the difference between?
options: A big and a small ship
A healthy company and a stressed one
items.why: "the difference between a healthy company and a stressed one."

items.q: How often do good trade companies watch their working capital?
items.why: "Good trade companies watch their working capital every week."

audio.text:
You asked why the treasury team watches working capital more closely than the profit number on paper. Good question — and the answer surprises a lot of people.

Profit tells you if the business is doing well over time. But it doesn't tell you if there's money in the bank today. A company can be profitable on paper and still run out of cash. And when you run out of cash, you can't pay salaries, you can't buy materials, and the business stops — even if it's 'profitable'.

Working capital is the money for right now. Think of it as the gap: money is coming in from customers, but slowly — they pay in sixty days. Meanwhile, money is going out fast — salaries every month, suppliers, tax.

If that gap gets too big, the company is stressed, even with good profit. So every week we ask: what's coming in, what's going out, and is there enough in between?

Profit is the story of the year. Working capital is the story of this week. And this week is the one that pays the salaries.

items.q: What does profit tell you?
options: If the business is doing well over time
If there's money in the bank today
items.why: "Profit tells you if the business is doing well over time."

items.q: What can happen to a company that is profitable on paper?
options: It can still run out of cash
items.why: "A company can be profitable on paper and still run out of cash."

items.q: Why is there a gap?
options: Money comes in slowly (60 days) but goes out fast (salaries, suppliers, tax)
items.why: "money is coming in from customers, but slowly… money is going out fast — salaries every month, suppliers, tax."

items.q: What does the team ask every week?
options: What's the profit for the year?
What's coming in, what's going out, and is there enough in between?
items.why: "what's coming in, what's going out, and is there enough in between?"

items.q: How does Harry sum it up?
options: Profit is this week; working capital is the year
Profit is the story of the year; working capital is the story of this week
items.why: "Profit is the story of the year. Working capital is the story of this week."

items.q: **Working capital** is…
options: the money needed to run the daily business
items.why: Working capital = capital de giro.

items.q: A **receivable** is…
options: money a customer will pay you
items.why: Receivable = conta a receber.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **___** is money the company must pay a supplier."
items.why: Payable = conta a pagar.

items.q: **Inventory** is…
items.why: Inventory = estoque.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **___** company always has enough cash for its bills."
items.why: Healthy = saudável.

items.q: "The company could **run out of** cash." To run out of means to…
items.why: Run out of = ficar sem.

items.q: "Profit **on paper** can hide a cash problem." On paper means…
items.why: On paper = no papel, na teoria.

items.q: "Money **comes in** from customers." To come in means to…
items.why: Come in = entrar.

items.q: "Money **goes out** to suppliers." To go out means to…
items.why: Go out = sair.

items.q: "If the gap is too big, the company is **stretched**." To be stretched means to…
options: be under strain with little to spare
items.why: Stretched = no limite, esticado.
